brief:
Settlers took control of livestock belonging to residents of Beita village today, the Ma'an news agency reported. The seizure marks the latest in a series of incidents involving property disputes between Palestinian communities and Jewish settlers in the occupied West Bank.

Beita, a village in the northern West Bank, has emerged as a focal point for confrontations over land and agricultural resources. Palestinian farmers in the area have faced repeated encroachments on their property and grazing lands as settlement expansion continues across the territory. The incident underscores ongoing friction between local residents and settler groups operating in the region.
title: Settlers seize livestock from Palestinian villagers in Beita
